name: apt

examples.does: Refresh the package lists from the configured sources
Packages that have a newer version
Install a package and what it needs
Upgrade installed packages (never removes any)
Every installed package
Installed version, available versions and where they come from (22.04: use apt-cache policy)
Remove a package, keep its config files
Remove a package and its config files
Remove packages nothing needs any more (read the list before saying yes)

pitfalls: The man page spells it --upgradeable; apt also accepts --upgradable.
In scripts use apt-get: apt's output format may change between releases.
In an air-gapped network, apt update needs an internal mirror in /etc/apt/sources.list.d/.

name: apt-get
summary: Package tool for scripts; also downloads .deb files
tasks: download a .deb for an offline server

examples.does: Install without the extra 'recommended' packages
Simulate an upgrade: show what would change
Download the .deb into the current folder without installing (carry it to an offline server)

pitfalls: apt-get download fetches one package only, not what it depends on. List those with apt-cache depends.

name: apt-cache
tasks: where does a package version come from

examples.does: Installed and candidate versions, and their sources
What a package needs
Installed packages that need this one
Packages with the word in their name

name: dpkg
summary: Low-level package tool: install .deb files, query what is installed

examples.does: Installed packages matching a name (ii = installed)
Files a package installed
Which package a file belongs to
Install a .deb file (dependencies must already be installed)
Finish package setups that were interrupted

pitfalls: dpkg -i does not fetch dependencies. With an internal mirror, sudo apt install ./package.deb does.

name: apt-mark

examples.does: Keep a package at its current version
Packages on hold
Allow upgrades again

pitfalls: Held packages also miss security fixes. Note why each one is held.
